feature.title: Ambassador is not owner.
body: The face is African. The cap table is not. In the second half of 2026 the pattern became impossible to miss — Tyla fronting Kate Spade, Tems an ambassador for Omega, Afrobeats carrying Louis Vuitton and Puma. Africa has never been more wanted by the world's brands.

But wanted is not the same as owned. Every one of those deals is an ambassadorship: the brand rents a face for a season and keeps the equity. Then watch the ceiling move — when Mbappé left Nike, he turned down roughly equal base money for an equity stake in On. A fee is spent once; a stake pays out every year the brand grows on the cultural capital you lent it.

It isn't a ceiling — it's a choice of structure, and Africans already built the other path: emPawa, Thebe Magugu, MaXhosa. The question for every star signing in 2027 is the Mbappé question: is there an equity line on this contract?
feature.pullQuote: Rent the asset and you get this season's cheque. Own it and you get the decade.
